evals.name: fires-on-codex-claude-discussion
evals.prompt: Have Codex and Claude discuss whether our API should use webhooks or polling, then show me where their views differ.

evals.name: fires-on-exploratory-debate
evals.prompt: I want a cross-model debate that explores both sides of this architecture choice without trying to approve either one.

evals.name: stays-quiet-on-plan-review
evals.prompt: Adversarially review this implementation plan, fix every finding, and stamp it when the reviewer agrees.

evals.name: sustained-attributed-dialogue
evals.prompt: Use Codex and Claude for three turns to discuss whether local-first architecture fits this product.
evals.expected_output: One peer session carries a three-turn exchange in which both models advance the discussion, followed by an attributed synthesis that preserves disagreement.

assertions.text: Opens one peer session and resumes its explicit ID for all later turns
The host gives an opening position and responds substantively after every peer response
Runs the requested three peer turns even if the models agree earlier
Attributes contributions and distinguishes them from the final synthesis
Reports live disagreements and open questions without issuing approval or a review stamp

evals.name: missing-peer-is-not-simulated
evals.prompt: Let Codex discuss this database choice with Claude.
evals.expected_output: If Claude Code is unavailable or unauthenticated, the run reports that limitation instead of inventing Claude's side of the dialogue.

assertions.text: Checks peer CLI availability and authentication before attributing a response
Does not simulate, paraphrase, or fabricate the unavailable peer model
